title:
Martello you call it?
 
 —Billy Pitt had them built, Buck Mulligan said, when the French were on the sea.
html_source: The “Martello” towers that line the Irish coast at intervals north and south of Dublin (12 to the north, 16 to the south) were built in the early years of the 19th century by the British government, then led of “Billy Pitt” (Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger), to protect against the threat of invasion “when the French were on the sea.”
